title: The Last Spire Revisited
premise: Wendell Kavanagh keeps the Last Spire's sealed gate in the Thornfell mountains, the only barrier between the free cities and the hollowed kingdom beyond. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, she is exposed by the very smugglers she once protected and dragged toward the capital, where she discovers the usurper is no man at all but the crown itself—a parasitic intelligence wearing kings for a century. To save the realm, Wendell must ally with Aldric, the true king's exiled brother, and unbind the current king from the thing on his head, even though doing so will cost her the gift that keeps her alive. She succeeds at the Spire's threshold, shattering the crown and sealing the gate with her own dying magic, surviving only because Aldric binds his loyalty—and his heart—to hers.
about_author: Ines Blackwood is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before trading ink for imagination. She writes fantasies about borders, both geographic and moral, from a cottage she insists is haunted.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell Kavanagh inspects the sealed gate of the Last Spire and records the season's smuggler routes, hiding her small gift of stone-sense from everyone, including her apprentice Tam. A tremor in the mountain hints the old wards are weakening. The beat is quiet unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Salt and Silver
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She trades passage secrets with smuggler captain Rhea Voss, an old friend whose loyalty has always been transactional. News arrives of the crown's proclamation: a hunt for the gifted, with silver for informants. The emotional beat is the first crack in Wendell's careful anonymity.

chapters.title: What the Stones Remember
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The apprentice, desperate for coin and resentful of Wendell's secrets, sells word of her gift to a crown rider. The chapter follows his guilt as he watches soldiers climb toward the Spire. The beat is betrayal born of love twisted into envy.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Soldiers take her at the gatehouse; Rhea refuses to intervene, choosing her crew over her friend. Wendell is marched out of the Thornfell, feeling the mountain's grief through her gift. The beat is abandonment and the shattering of her self-sufficient identity.

chapters.title: The Road of Collars
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, chained in a prisoner column. She meets other captured gifted, including a healer named Sefa who teaches her that power shared is power doubled. When soldiers execute a boy whose gift flares, Wendell vows to stop running. The beat is grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Without a Crown
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The exiled prince ambushes the prisoner column to free the gifted, expecting a weapon and finding instead a stubborn gatekeeper. Wendell saves his life when his strike falters. Their first exchange is barbed; the beat is reluctant mutual recognition.

chapters.title: Ashmarket
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The rebels shelter in the burned free city of Ashmarket, where Wendell sees what a century of the crown's hunger has cost. Aldric reveals the truth: his brother King Edran wears the crown, and the crown wears him. The beat is horror at the scope of the enemy.

chapters.title: Lessons in Borrowed Fire
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The gifted refugees train together, and Wendell learns to push her stone-sense beyond touch—reading the mountain's memory of the Spire's founding. She glimpses the crown's origin: it was forged to bind, not to rule. The beat is wonder shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Summons
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. A traitor in camp delivers an offer from the crown: amnesty for all gifted if Aldric kneels and delivers Wendell. The camp fractures. Wendell overhears rebels voting to consider it. The beat is isolation—she is a bargaining chip even among allies.

chapters.title: Rhea's Price
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Rhea Voss arrives under a parley flag, confessing she informed on Wendell to save her crew from conscription. Wendell must choose between fury and forgiveness, and chooses a third path: Rhea's ships for the rebels' cause. The beat is loyalty renegotiated, not restored.

chapters.title: The King in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric recounts his last meeting with Edran—how his brother wept behind eyes that were not his own, begging for a knife. Aldric has carried that failure for ten years. He and Wendell, both keepers of guilty secrets, find common ground. The beat is intimacy through shared shame.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Gate
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The camp traitor opens the pass to crown riders; the camp burns. Tam appears among the soldiers—now a crown ward, hollow-eyed. Wendell spares him, and the choice marks her. The beat is the cost of mercy in wartime.

chapters.title: Into the Hollow Kingdom
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The survivors flee through the Thornfell's deep roads, guided by Wendell's stone-sense, pursued by the usurper's general Veyra. Sefa witnesses Wendell burning her gift brighter than is safe to hold the passes open. The beat is awe and the first glimpse of the price to come.

chapters.title: Veyra's Mercy
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The general, herself quietly gifted, interrogates a captured rebel and reveals the crown's endgame: it intends to consume every gifted mind to sustain its failing host. Veyra hesitates, planting the seed of her defection. The beat is the enemy's humanity.

chapters.title: The Spire's Secret
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the Last Spire, Wendell's gift unlocks the founders' vault: the crown can be unbound only at the gate it was forged to seal, by a keeper willing to pour their gift into the wards and burn it out forever. The beat is the terrible clarity of sacrifice.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Living
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric refuses to let Wendell pay the price and proposes a doomed alternative assault on the capital. They argue through the night and end in each other's arms, both knowing duty will win. The beat is love declared in the shadow of loss.

chapters.title: The March on the Capital
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The rebels and Rhea's smuggler fleet converge on the capital while Veyra, having freed her prisoners, turns her legion to the rebel banner. Tam, escaped, brings the palace's gate-words as his penance. The beat is improbable hope before the storm.

chapters.title: The Crown's Voice
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. In the throne room, the crown speaks through Edran's mouth, offering Wendell her heart's desire—restored gift, safe mountains—if she walks away. Edran, surfacing for one moment, begs his brother to finish it. The beat is temptation and heartbreak entwined.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, the climax. At the Spire's threshold, Wendell pours her gift into the ancient wards while Sefa and the gifted shield her from the crown's onslaught. The crown shatters; Edran dies free, whispering thanks. Wendell's gift gutters out, and she collapses as the gate seals. The beat is triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: The Quiet After
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam keeps vigil over the dying Wendell, atoning in silence, while Aldric refuses the throne the rebels press on him until Wendell wakes. The beat is penance, patience, and the community forged from the hunt's survivors.

chapters.title: What the Gate Keeps
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Giftless but alive, Wendell finds the mountain still faintly answers her—not magic now, but memory. Aldric offers her not a crown but a partnership: rebuilding the free cities with the gate between them and the hollow kingdom. The beat is love chosen freely over duty imposed.

chapters.title: The Last Spire Revisited
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. One year later, Wendell walks the smugglers' roads as a road-warden, Rhea's ships in the harbor and Tam at her side as the new gatekeeper. At the sealed Spire she leaves flowers for Edran and Sefa, gone to heal the south. The beat is hard-won peace, and a final tremor in the stone—unexplained, patient, waiting.
